experiments.title: Item coverage floor reads each item's own Source and runs on flagged gates
experiments.baseline: Item coverage on the last 4 episodes of each established news show: Tesla 25-67%, SpaceX 0-43%, FF 7-33%, M&A 0-46%, Omni View 0%, MIT 0-20%, MAB 0-100%; the floor added 1 verified claim in 24 episodes. The repair call answered [] on Tesla Ep624 and SpaceX Ep120 (2026-10-04 logs): it asked for a page from memory. 4 of those 24 (and 3 of Planetterrian's last 4) were still failing after the first repair and got no floor at all.
experiments.target: source_integrity_item_coverage_pct median >= 50 on Tesla, SpaceX, M&A, Omni View and MIT over 14 days; coverage_repair_added > 0 on >= 60% of the episodes where the floor ran; the network claims page's verified share does not fall.
experiments.criteria: Hit = all three. coverage_repair_grounded high but _added near 0 = the model will not quote (read the "item coverage floor" log line's offered / rejected counts before touching the prompt); grounded low = the run's fetched copy is thin on those shows (fetch_full_text), not the floor. A verified-share drop means added entries are failing on re-verification and the floor is not only adding.
experiments.notes: Replay without the model on six Oct 3-4 flagship digests: 29 of 43 uncovered sourced items got a passage from their own Source URL by HTTP alone (the runner also holds the fetched copy). The mechanical check is unchanged; entries are added only when each verifies, and the result is kept only when the gate verifies more and gets no worse. Metadata only: the ledger and the claims panels change, no prose and no audio.

experiments.criteria: OPERATOR OVERRIDE of the July-31 digests-stay-on-4.3 decision (explicitly directed 2026-08-18, risks acknowledged: 4.6's confident-hallucination profile is unmeasured for this network). REVERT TRIGGERS, checked daily via the audit, decided at readout: (1) any invented number/ticker/price in an MIT script — immediate one-line revert (model: grok-4.3 in _defaults.yaml); (2) reviewer FACTUAL_ERRORS rate clearly above baseline across shows; (3) fetch tool-calls (x_search/web_search) failing on 4.6. Also A/B-listen the first post-merge episode on 2-3 shows per landmine #17 — every script's prose changes with this merge.
experiments.notes: Everything moved together: digest/fetch, scripts (dp_pod's 4.5 and MIT's 4.6 pins removed — superseded/absorbed), synth, titles, reviewer, review agent, restock; refusal fallback repointed grok-4.20-reasoning -> grok-4.3 (different snapshot than the new primary, retires the aging 4.20 dependency). Translation was already pinned 4.6 same-day. ~+$22-25/mo at current volume. REVERTED SAME DAY (2026-08-18, operator-directed): the trigger was OPERATIONAL, not on the registered list — 4.6 digest latency ran 5-10x 4.3 on every show measured (planetterrian 44s -> 420s, MAB 36s -> 242s, dp_pod 55s -> 225s, first_principles 36s -> 205s) and on the four largest digest prompts (tesla, spacex, omni_view, modern_investing) requests exceeded the 300s client timeout or were server-disconnected. Nested SDK+tenacity retries amplified each stall into a 41-45 min burn; 7 of 12 shows failed on day one (2026-08-18 07:37-10:33 UTC). Rolled back to grok-4.3 everywhere except the translation pin (already 4.6 via the alias freeze, small chunks, no timeouts observed). The hallucination-profile question is UNANSWERED — the experiment never reached an editorial readout. Any retry follows docs/model_upgrade_playbook.md: one show first, digest-latency gate before network-wide.

experiments.title: grok-4.6 staged trial — dp_pod script, synth, reviewer (FPD+UC arms withdrawn 2026-08-27)
experiments.baseline: All stages on grok-4.3 after the same-day revert of the network-wide 4.6 upgrade. dp_pod on 4.3: zero exclamation points in 27/30 episodes, Ep22 65% verbatim digest paste. FPD/UC: the accepted grok-4.3 narrative-length plateau (briefs 848-1116w vs 1600 ask). FPD/UC digest latency on 4.3: ~30-50s.
experiments.target: dp_pod scripts follow the delivery spec (exclamations/voice tags present, shingle overlap with the digest clearly below the 65%/42% worst cases). FPD/UC briefs come off the 4.3 plateau without the banned podcast-side retries. No latency regressions: stage durations in metrics_ep*.json stay under 50% of NERRA_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (600s) and zero 'Slow LLM completion' warnings after week one.
experiments.criteria: Operator-directed staged rollout per docs/model_upgrade_playbook.md (the first trial run under it). SCOPE: dp_pod llm.podcast_model ONLY (digest stays 4.3); first_principles + unintended_consequences whole-show (narrative — the brief is model-knowledge prose); synth_model + reviewer_model in _defaults. Every daily NEWS show's digest/fetch stays grok-4.3. REVERT TRIGGERS, any one suffices, revert = delete the named pin: (1) an invented fact/date/name in an FPD or UC story (these are factual histories) — judged against the other shows' FACTUAL_ERRORS under the SAME 4.6 reviewer, never against pre-08-18 history (the reviewer instrument changed this date too); (2) a digest/script stage exceeding ~300s repeatedly or any request timeout on a trial show; (3) a missed episode attributable to the model; (4) dp_pod A/B-listen verdict against the 4.6 scripts (landmine #17 — prose changes with the model).
experiments.notes: Follow-up to network-grok-46-upgrade (reverted for latency, not quality — the quality question was never answered). Trial shows were picked benefit-over-risk: dp_pod's dialogue writing is its product and its 4.3 failures are documented writing-model limitations; FPD/UC have no news fetch so a stronger model is the only sanctioned length/depth lever; synth + reviewer are analysis-stage, operator-gated or non-published. The four biggest-prompt news shows (tesla, spacex, omni_view, MIT) stay OFF 4.6 — highest hallucination stakes and the four that timed out on outage day. NERRA_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS raised 300 -> 600 in run-show.yml (worst-case per stage 3 x 600s = 30 min, still under the 50-min watchdog). Cost: ~+$3-5/mo at trial scope.

experiments.title: Story-driven scene briefs — the pictures follow the narration
experiments.target: Viewer complaints about imagery not matching the subject stop; long-form hold at 5% and Shorts AVP up. Mechanism: one Grok text call per episode writes a concrete, photographable scene per STORY (engine/scene_briefs.py); those briefs LEAD every Grok Imagine prompt (the static image_queries — 'cybertruck', 'supercharger' — used to lead, so every Tesla episode shipped the same four pictures); one fresh 16:9 scene per story (cap 8, was a fixed 4) keyed to its chapter for the scheduler; the library blend is back to 8 and ON-TOPIC ONLY (>=1 shared token with hook + chapter titles) instead of padding with random older images.
experiments.notes: Cost: +~4 images/episode at $0.02 (+$0.08/ep, ~+$30/mo network) + one ~$0.005 text call. Per-show opt-out scene_briefs_enabled; counts via scenes_per_episode / short_scenes_per_episode. Render/metadata only (outside landmine #17). First A/B-eyeball: compare a tesla + spacex + FF episode's scenes_ep*/ against the digest headlines. 2026-09-09 EARLY READ (lag-aware, 09-03..06 vs 08-27..31; several changes landed together, so this is a joint read with hook-first titles and the 2K sources): EN views/day roughly doubled (WoW +55.7%, 15,680 vs 10,070), RU +17.1%, Shorts AVP EN 43 -> 50% (median), FR 44 -> 52%; per-video EN long 30 -> 78 views, EN Short 12 -> 25. Biggest movers: MAB Shorts 10 -> 227 views/video, Planetterrian Shorts 9 -> 287, FF long 28 -> 116, SpaceX long 80 -> 277. Long-form AVP did NOT move (EN 14 -> 10-14%) and the open cliff sits at 0.48-0.49 hold at 5% — the retention metric this entry is scored on is still the open question for 09-23.

Vancouver and Collingwood Ep1 (runs 35816762370 / 35816778529) died in the digest stage — the 10-token pre-flight ping timed out at 30 s, then three digest attempts each hung ~260 s until xAI dropped the connection. No committed credit file anywhere records a grok-4.7 completion: omni_view's script-stage pin fell back to grok-4.3 on its first run (the script stage has always had that fallback). The operator wants 4.7 on the new shows, so the pins STAY and a run whose pinned model fails the ping or the digest call switches to grok-4.3 for the rest of the process (engine.generator.switch_to_network_default, guards tests/test_pinned_model_fallback_2026_09_23.py). The resilience pass (grok-47-resilience-2026-09-24) is what makes this experiment readable; its live metric is the fallback share.

experiments.target: By 10-21: capture.by_source holds at least one row, select_personal_upsell appears in api/ga4_stats.json, and api/member_metrics.json reports a paid_active_total. Those are existence checks on purpose — NOT a conversion rate. At 282 sessions and 5 subscribers in 28 days no rate can move measurably in a month, and scoring this on conversion would be scoring noise. Whether anyone subscribes is the next question, and it needs these three to be answerable at all.
experiments.notes: The upsell event is a SEPARATE GA4 report from conversions, not a wider filter: build_funnel._captures() sums every row of the conversions report into signup_events_total, so an engagement event in that list would have reported an intention as a subscriber. Named vocabularies (CONVERSION_EVENTS / ENGAGEMENT_EVENTS) so the next event a template fires is not silently dropped — this is the fourth instance of the "a result key is not a metric" class after grok_image_px_max, caption_track_uploaded and the OP3 prefix. The Worker's duplicate path now merges tags as a UNION, because PATCH replaces the array and sending only the wanted tags would strip a member's show subscriptions on their next footer signup — a data loss that would look exactly like a working signup; every merge failure still reports the subscribe as successful, since an attribution tag is not worth a 502 on someone's signup. member_metrics is counts and show histograms ONLY, never a name, city, email or feed token: the admin endpoint returns first_name and city, and at five members that identifies a person, in a file committed to a public repo. free_accounts, mrr_usd and trialing are null because no wired source can answer them — Stripe is read by nothing in this repo. Unmeasured is null, never 0, and a run with no token leaves real counts alone rather than overwriting them. The forms render the capture tag from a Jinja global fed by engine.funnel, never a literal, per CLAUDE.md's second standing rule. No prompt and no audio changed. Guards: tests/test_capture_measurement_2026_09_21.py.
